title: Branch-and-Commit for Frozen RL Agents: When and Where to Spend Test-Time Compute
abstract: arXiv:2611.13003v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reinforcement learning agents are often deployed with policies that cannot be retrained or modified. In digital environments whose states can be copied and resumed, an operator has another option: sample several continuations from the current state, evaluate them, and continue from the endpoint of the selected branch. We call this procedure branch-and-commit. We study when it improves return, what produces the improvement, and where its computational budget should be spent. Across four environments, two frozen policies, five continuation verifiers, and a model-free selection rule, we find that the benefit of branching depends on dispersion: the difference between the best candidate return and the mean candidate return. Branching provides no benefit in low-dispersion settings, while increasing return by 12.8% in our main Craftax-Medium setting. translated_title: 面向冻结强化学习智能体的分支与提交方法：何时以及在哪里投入测试时计算
translated_abstract: 强化学习智能体在部署时，其策略通常无法重新训练或修改。在状态可以被复制和恢复的数字环境中，操作者还有另一种选择：从当前状态采样多个候选延续，对它们进行评估，然后从所选分支的端点继续执行。我们将这一过程称为“分支与提交”。我们研究了它何时能改善回报、改善的来源是什么，以及其计算预算应该花在哪里。通过在四个环境、两个冻结策略、五个延续验证器和一个无模型选择规则上进行实验，我们发现分支带来的收益取决于离散度：即最佳候选回报与平均候选回报之间的差异。在低离散度的设置中，分支不会带来任何收益；而在我们的主要Craftax-Medium设置中，回报提升了12.8%。这一收益的大部分并非来自选择更好的动作，而是来自在不同状态之间进行选择。
tldr: 该论文提出针对冻结RL智能体的“分支与提交”方法，发现分支收益取决于候选回报的离散度——低离散度时无收益，高离散度时可提升回报12.8%，且收益主要来自在不同状态间选择而非选择更优动作。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes "branch-and-commit" for frozen RL agents, showing that branching benefits depend on candidate return dispersion—with no gain in low-dispersion settings but up to 12.8% return improvement in high-dispersion settings—and that most gains come from selecting among different states rather than better actions.
